warnings.warning: The equal weight and 0.85 zone threshold are assumed choices; reuse must say under the selected weight and threshold rather than claim a universal optimum.
The 0.3123 scaling is unexplained and the output is a grip-acceleration proxy, not measured comfort or hand force.
The six-point restitution fit and floor remain source-faithful but do not establish predictive validity outside the fitted positions.
The displayed corked-bat center-inertia transformation has the previously recorded parallel-axis error; downstream cork magnitudes are retained as source evidence, not endorsed results.
The transferred aluminum restitution curve uses a wood baseline inconsistent with the earlier fitted data, so material comparisons remain conditional.

global_organization_chain: Summary defines the decision object and previews the wood, cork, and aluminum branches.
Introduction separates competing meanings before fixing the two-criterion operational definition.
Assumptions and definitions bound the baseline object and collision terms.
The wood branch derives the objective, comfort proxy, collision response, parameters, result, and sensitivity in dependency order.
The cork branch reuses the wood core after a geometry-to-mass-to-swing transformation and closes with comparative outputs and decision meaning.
The aluminum branch repeats the same parameter-to-solution-to-comparison grammar for a material counterfactual.
Strengths, implementable future mechanisms, and present limitations precede audience recommendations.

main_argument_chains.claim: The modeled sweet spot is an interior compromise rather than the bat end.
support_steps: Define the construct through exit speed and grip-response criteria.
Derive the two component functions from rigid-body comfort and collision relations.
Combine them in one weighted objective and compare its optimum with the single-criterion points and bat end.
Sweep preference, mass, and swing speed to separate location stability from performance change.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Report the selected location only under the stated weights, parameterization, and proxy boundary.

main_argument_chains.claim: Cork depth can be evaluated by modifying mass properties and reusing the common objective.
support_steps: Turn the contested performance belief into a corked-versus-uncorked comparison question.
Map cork depth to mass, center, inertia, and empirical swing speed.
Substitute the scenario parameters into the common comfort and collision model.
Compare location, speed, comfort, and zone width before discussing the rule.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Keep the branch architecture as a reusable pattern while treating its quantitative magnitudes as conditional on the retained inertia warning.

main_argument_chains.claim: A common output grammar supports a direct wood-versus-aluminum comparison.
support_steps: Represent the aluminum alternative with hollow coaxial geometry and declared material parameters.
Reuse the common objective and report comfortable, maximum-speed, and compromise points.
Compare exit speed and sweet-zone width on the paper's stated scales.
Perturb wall thickness and separate output direction from the feasibility boundary.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the matched comparison sequence, but keep performance and policy conclusions conditional on common calibration and coupling assumptions.

main_argument_chains.claim: The paper remains coherent by reusing one objective, visual grammar, and result-to-action close across three branches.
support_steps: Preview the three branches in the Summary in body order.
Use parameter substitution, aligned tables and curves, numerical contrast, and decision meaning in each branch.
Place strengths, future mechanisms, and limitations before recommendations.
Close with parallel user actions and a safety boundary.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reuse this organization when multiple design branches share a real model interface and common decision metrics.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Force diagrams align the translational and rotational mechanics with the nearby equations.
A family of preference curves and a corresponding optimum-location plot make the decision tradeoff immediately visible.
The cork cross-section diagram fixes the interpretation of depth, diameter, filler, and omitted cap before equations are introduced.
Tables and aligned curves expose nonmonotonic cork-depth output that would be easy to hide in prose.
Wood and aluminum response curves use a consistent comparison grammar and are followed by explicit percentage statements.
Wall-thickness plots communicate local sensitivity clearly, but the visual response cannot validate mechanisms absent from the equations.
